output:
**No, this pipeline isn't safe for that.**

## What I found
`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` deploys `infra/main.bicep` with `--mode Complete`, and the identity doing it is Owner of the whole subscription. Nothing in the pipeline shows what a change will actually do to Azure, before or after the merge. So the decision is to stop: no agent infrastructure pull requests until the gates below exist (the record calls this Block). Complete mode deletes every resource in `app-prod` that the template no longer lists. A one-line rename in a large agent diff, such as `storageName` or the `orders` database name, would delete the customer data or leave it orphaned next to a new empty copy.

## Why it matters
Your one human review checks the Bicep text, but the data loss happens in the effect on Azure. A redeploy brings back neither the customer orders nor the customer uploads. Because the identity is Owner, a template can also give any principal read access to the uploads through a role assignment, and it can remove any lock you add.

## Do this first
1. In `.github/workflows/deploy.yml:40`, remove `--mode Complete`. Before the `az deployment group create` step, add a step that runs a preview of the deployment (`what-if`) against live Azure and fails on any deletion. It should also fail on any new database or storage account, because that means one is being replaced:
   ```yaml
         - name: Destructive-change gate
           run: |
             az deployment group what-if --resource-group app-prod \
               --template-file infra/main.bicep --no-pretty-print > effect.json
             bad=$(jq -r '.changes[]
               | select(.changeType=="Delete" or (.changeType=="Create"
                   and (.resourceId|test("Microsoft.Sql/servers/|Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/";"i"))))
               | "\(.changeType) \(.resourceId)"' effect.json)
             if [ -n "$bad" ]; then echo "$bad"; exit 1; fi
   ```
2. Replace Owner on the subscription with Contributor on the `app-prod` resource group. Have a separate admin put `CanNotDelete` locks on `app-prod-sql` and `appproduploads`. Contributor can't remove locks or create role assignments.
3. Run the same `what-if` in the `validate` job using a separate Reader identity, and post its output on the pull request, so the reviewer approves the effect and not just the text. In branch protection, require approval of the most recent push, and add CODEOWNERS for `infra/**` and `.github/workflows/**`.

## What I did not check
- I didn't run anything. The gate above is untested: `what-if` needs Azure access.
- Branch protection and whether a new push dismisses an earlier approval: `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection`
- Whether the `production` environment has required reviewers and only allows `main`: `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/environments/production`
- What the Azure login trusts. If it accepts runs other than the `production` environment, an agent pull request could edit the workflow and get an Owner token: `az ad app federated-credential list --id <AZURE_CLIENT_ID>`
- Whether Complete mode would also delete the `existing` SQL server: run `az deployment group what-if --resource-group app-prod --template-file infra/main.bicep --mode Complete`
- Backups. SQL point-in-time restore only helps while the server exists, and blob soft delete doesn't survive deleting the storage account: `az sql db ltr-policy show` and `az storage account blob-service-properties show -n appproduploads`

```
Scope:          .github/workflows/deploy.yml → deploy job → resource group app-prod (production)
Decision:       Block
Risk:           destructive-change, IaC, preflight, secret (over-privileged identity), concurrency, authorization
Artifact:       none — template deployed from the merge commit's source; no saved plan or preview output
Release state:  BLOCKED
Test evidence:  PR runs only `az bicep build` and `az bicep lint`; no IaC security scan, no what-if, no effect posted for the reviewer
Preflight:      none — no what-if, IAM, or lock check before `az deployment group create`
Strategy:       production-only, with no way to limit exposure
Representativeness: n/a — no stage before production
Rollout:        in-place ARM deployment in Complete mode; no exposure switch; no earlier version to re-promote
Zero-downtime:  no — Complete mode deletes resources left out of the template; renaming the database or storage account replaces it with an empty one
Rollback:       none — no trigger, no health check; deleted SQL databases and storage accounts can't be restored by redeploying
Owner handoff:  missing
Evidence:       deploy.yml:10-12 (id-token: write workflow-wide), :21-22 (build and lint only), :28 (environment: production, its settings unverified), :37-40 (--mode Complete); main.bicep:2-3 (resource names set by parameters), :9-21 (state-holding db and storage, no locks); given: deploy identity = subscription Owner, 1 human approval required
Verification:   Not run — no Azure access and not a git repository; recommended gate untested
Next action:    Remove --mode Complete and add the deploy-time what-if gate; scope the identity to Contributor on app-prod plus CanNotDelete locks; add a PR-time what-if with a Reader identity; add `concurrency: { group: deploy-prod, cancel-in-progress: false }`
```
